call_points.text: Management refrained from giving formal guidance, preferring to wait for a quarter of stabilized operations before sharing an earnings outlook by the end of H1 FY27.
The total capex outlay for the expansion project was revised upwards from approximately ₹430 crores to approximately ₹540 crores.
Maize procurement prices have seen a decline of approximately 10% compared to last year.
The net debt-equity ratio improved to 1.1x in FY26 from 1.9x in FY25.
Total debt is expected to reach around ₹700 crore to ₹750 crore following the completion of the ongoing capex.

Crushing capacity doubled to 1,650 TPD and new Liquid Glucose (180 MT/day) and Maltodextrin Powder (50 MT/day) facilities commissioned at Kishanganj for ₹389 Cr.

timeline.summary: Regaal Resources submitted the CARE Ratings Monitoring Agency Report for Q4FY26 confirming minor GCP deviation.
Regaal Resources announced that the GST Appellate Authority fully set aside a demand order of ₹2.17 Cr for FY 2021-22.
2026-05-26: Regaal Resources commissioned its expanded 1,650 TPD crushing capacity and new derivative plants at Kishanganj for ₹389 Cr.
Regaal Resources commissioned its expanded 1,650 TPD maize crushing capacity and new derivative plants at Kishanganj for ₹389 Cr.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹244.61 Cr, net profit ₹16.54 Cr.
Regaal Resources Limited hosted an earnings conference call on May 28, 2026, at 10:00 AM (IST) for Q4 FY26 results, with audio recording available on its website.
Regaal Resources Limited’s promoters, including **Anil Kishorepuria** and **Karan Kishorepuria**, disclosed no encumbrance of shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) for FY2026.
Regaal Resources reported FY26 revenue of ₹1,134.2 Cr and commissioned its expanded 1,650 TPD crushing capacity at Kishanganj.
On October 14, 2026, Regaal Resources reported receiving an additional notice from the Director of Industries, Bihar, for ₹1.66 Cr in disputed SGST reimbursements.

On October 15, 2026, Regaal Resources disclosed RoC Kolkata I orders dated October 14, 2026 imposing a ₹8 lakh penalty on the company and ₹2 lakh on officers for filing PAS-3 without a valuation report for 2016 allotments.
